title: Tatting-style lace edging
excerpt: A ring-and-chain edging in lace weight yarn that imitates the look of tatted lace. Circular rings of trebles alternate with chain bridges along the strip.
sourceNotes: A crochet interpretation of tatting using small treble rings and chain bridges to mimic the characteristic ring-and-chain structure of shuttled lace.
aliases: tatting look edging crochet lace weight

glossaryTerms.definition: A small closed ring worked by making a magic ring and filling it with trebles, then joining with a slip stitch. It imitates the shuttle ring of tatted lace.
A short chain arc worked between two rings to connect them, mimicking the chain element of tatting.

crochet.finishedSizeText: Edging strip to any length required, approx. 3 cm wide.

Work a foundation dc row to the required length. Fasten off.

Join yarn at the start of the foundation row. Work first ring: magic ring, 12 tr into ring, join with slip stitch, picot at the joining point. Work chain bridge: ch 6, sl st into the 4th dc of the foundation row. Work next ring as before, joining the first picot of the new ring to the last picot of the previous ring. Continue alternating rings and bridges across the length. Fasten off.
Sew the foundation row to your fabric edge with the tapestry needle. Weave in all ends.
